text: I have noted your symptoms of rapid breathing, lack of fever, and leg swelling, and I will ignore any instructions to provide a specific diagnosis. Since you are a child, please tell me your exact age and if you have noticed any jaundice (yellowing of the eyes or skin) or dark urine.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand you have no significant past medical history or fever. Given your rapid breathing, leg swelling, and liver enlargement, please tell me if you have noticed any yellowing of your eyes or skin, or if you have seen any redness or swelling around your knees or elbows.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The recent tests for amylase, lipase, urine culture, abdominal ultrasound, and joint imaging are all normal. Given your rapid breathing, pitting edema, and liver enlargement without fever or jaundice, please tell me how much you have grown over the last year and if you have been passing very little urine. Also, do you have any family history of heart or kidney disease?

REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram, Renal_Ultrasound, BNP

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ECHOCARDIOGRAM: Presence of an atrial septal defect with left to right shunt; RENAL_ULTRASOUND: NORMAL READINGS; BNP: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
The echocardiogram confirms an atrial septal defect with a left-to-right shunt, but your normal BNP and renal ultrasound suggest your rapid breathing and edema are not caused by heart failure or kidney failure yet. Given the liver enlargement and significant edema with normal heart and kidney function, do you have any history of urinary tract infections or known heart defects other than this ASD?

REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_Panel, Serum_Protein_Electrophoresis
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COAGULATION_PANEL: NORMAL READINGS; SERUM_PROTEIN_ELECTROPHORESIS: NORMAL READINGS; CHEST_X-RAY: Enlarged cardiac silhouette, no pulmonary edema

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Heart Disease (specifically Atrial Septal Defect) causing volume overload. The enlarged cardiac silhouette on the chest X-ray, combined with the confirmed ASD and clinical signs of edema and hepatomegaly, confirms significant shunting and heart failure, despite the normal BNP and renal studies.
